age.evidence: young (2 months, n = 21), adult (9 months, n = 38), and old (12-18 months, n = 17) animals

dosing.evidence: The study used high-purity LSD dissolved in ultrapure water... Each animal received 1 or 3 daily intraperitoneal injections of saline or LSD (0.065 mg/kg, 0.13 mg/kg, and 0.39 mg/kg)

group_housing.evidence: Before injection, animals were housed with other animals... After that, each animal was housed in cages with 4 other animals.

assays.assay_description: Cubic arena (44 x 44 x 41 cm) with two objects fixed 11 cm apart. 3 days habituation (10 min/day), training session with two identical objects, test session 30 min later with one familiar and one novel object. Discrimination index calculated from time exploring novel vs familiar object.

application_type.evidence: Each animal received 1 or 3 daily intraperitoneal injections of saline or LSD

setup_habituation.evidence: For three days preceding the task, animals were habituated for 10 min in the arena.

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were placed facing the same arena wall, with the objects on their back

food_restriction.evidence: No food in the testing arena (standard NOR apparatus)

water_restriction.evidence: No water in the testing arena (standard NOR apparatus)

time_to_assay.evidence: After the last dose, animals were given a short (3 days) or long (9 days) washout interval, to characterize the timeframe of the drug's effect.

sample_size.evidence: Wistar male rats (n = 76)... young (2 months, n = 21), adult (9 months, n = 38), and old (12-18 months, n = 17)

outcomes.summary: LSD pre-treatment (0.13 mg/kg) significantly increased time exploring the novel object in the test session. The effect was greatest in adult rats at the intermediate dose of 0.13 mg/kg, with daily 3-day dosing being less effective than a single dose. The efficacy correlated negatively with age and weight, though no significant LSD-Age interaction was observed.
outcomes.statistics: LSD effect: p = 0.03; Age effect: p = 0.05; LSD-Age effect: p = 0.42
outcomes.evidence: In the test session, LSD dosing increased the time exploring the novel object... a maximum of novel object preference was found for the intermediate dose of 0.13 mg/kg

B1_num_measures.evidence: time exploring novel object, time exploring familiar object, discrimination index (DI)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Single total/discrimination index over the session; no within-session time-course analysis

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural sequences or transitions reported

B4_ethological.evidence: preference for the novel object indicates... the animal is intrinsically motivated to explore the novel object (i.e. curious about the unknown) - natural exploratory behaviour

B5_social.evidence: Animals were tested alone in the arena

B6_cognitive.evidence: novel object preference task to measure the subacute effects of LSD pre-treatment on hippocampus-dependent memory processes

B7_automated_classification.evidence: No automated behavioural classification software described beyond video recording

B8_multivariate.evidence: Analyses performed with univariate ANOVAs; no PCA or multivariate method

E1_environment_type.evidence: cubic arena (44 cm x 44 cm x 41 cm)

E3_bedding.evidence: No bedding described in the testing arena

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material in the arena

D2_session_duration.evidence: Exact session duration not explicitly stated; habituation was 10 min and standard NOR sessions are typically short

judge_notes: Only the rat novel object preference task is a scorable in vivo rodent behavioural assay. Brain organoid proteomics, human behavioural tasks, and the computational model are excluded per rubric.
Vehicle resolved to 'water' based on Methods: 'high-purity LSD dissolved in ultrapure water... for brain organoids and rats'.

Schedule scored as 'acute' since the primary effective protocol was a single dose; the 3-daily-dose variant is still <=7 doses and the assay reports a single dose as most effective. Either 'acute' or 'repeated' is defensible; chose 'acute' to match the dominant finding.
B4 scored Yes (exploration of objects is natural exploratory behaviour scored as a distinct act) per modal candidate position.
D3 scored 1 (single recording day): training and test occurred 30 min apart on the same day; habituation days had no data collection reported.
